To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the absence of complex N- or O-glycosylation in the oocyte results in delayed pre- and peri-implantation embryo development, reduced ovulation rate, and premature ovarian failure in mice.
a lack of complex glycosylation in oocytes during oogenesis results in impaired embryo development in vivo and delayed implantation leading to a small litter.
the lack of complex N and O-glycosylation of oocytes in vivo impairs embryo development and viability and leads to delayed implantation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that control the early development of the embryo, and the role of the oocyte in these events.
the role of glycans in the female reproductive tract and their effect on early embryo development.
understanding the role of glycans in mammalian development and their potential use in assisted reproductive technologies (ART).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lack of complex N-glycans and O-glycosylation in oocytes results in impaired early embryo development, delayed implantation and reduced litter size.
a lack of complex glycans during oocyte maturation impairs embryo viability and implantation in vivo.
the absence of complex N- (and to a lesser extent O-) glycans on oocytes and zygotes results in delayed embryo development and implantation, and a small litter size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ZP plays an essential role for embryo development and implantation, and that complex N- and/or O-glycose chains in the ZP are essential for this function.
the lack of N-and O-glycanylation in the oocyte leads to delayed preimplantations development, which in turn delays implantation, and ultimately leads to premature ovarian failure (Fig. 6).

a lack of complex O-glycains in oocytes leads to a reduction in the number of oocytes available for ovulation and a lack of complex glycan in both oocytes and embryos results in a reduction in the viability of the oocytes and embryos.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absence of complex N- or O-glycanylation in oocytes has a dramatic effect on the development and survival of the embryo, leading to a small litter and premature ovarian failure.
the ZP is critical for embryo viability and development.
the absence of ZP3, a protein that is essential to normal ZP structure, is not sufficient to explain the reduced ovulation rate and the small litter size in Mgat1;Galt1 double mutant mice.
